title: RxJS and Observables
summary: Streams of values over time — the foundation behind HttpClient and forms.
heading: RxJS and Observables

blocks.text: You've been using Observables already — HttpClient returns them and you call .subscribe(). An Observable is a stream of values that arrive over time: it might emit one value (an HTTP response), many (every click or keystroke), or none. RxJS is the library of tools for working with these streams.

blocks.caption: An observable emits values over time until it completes.

cards.title: Observable
cards.code:
// many values, runs on subscribe
http.get('/api').subscribe(r => ...)

blocks.text: Observables are lazy: nothing happens until you subscribe. A Promise runs as soon as it's created.
Make simple observables with of (a fixed set of values) or from (an array or promise). Subscribe to receive each value.

blocks.label: create + subscribe

blocks.text: Long-lived streams keep emitting, so you must stop listening to avoid leaks. In components, takeUntilDestroyed() cleans up automatically.

blocks.label: auto cleanup

blocks.text: Operators transform a stream. You chain them inside .pipe(...) — like array map/filter, but for values arriving over time.

blocks.label: map / filter / tap

blocks.text: Each operator returns a new observable; the original stream is untouched.
In templates, the async pipe subscribes for you and unsubscribes when the component is destroyed — no manual subscribe needed.

blocks.label: component + template

blocks.text: When one stream should trigger another — like a search box firing an HTTP request per keystroke — use switchMap. It cancels the previous inner request when a new value arrives, exactly what a type-ahead needs.

blocks.label: type-ahead search

blocks.text: Relatives: mergeMap (run all), concatMap (one after another), exhaustMap (ignore new while busy). switchMap is the go-to for search and navigation.
Run several requests together with forkJoin (wait for all, like Promise.all), or react whenever any of several streams changes with combineLatest.

blocks.label: forkJoin (parallel)

blocks.text: A Subject is both an observable and an emitter — you can push values into it. A BehaviorSubject also remembers the latest value and hands it to new subscribers, which makes it handy for simple shared state in a service.

blocks.label: BehaviorSubject

blocks.text: Today, signals are often simpler for state; use observables for streams and async events. Bridge them with toSignal(obs$) and toObservable(sig).

items: An Observable is a lazy stream of values over time; subscribe to receive them.
The async pipe subscribes and cleans up for you in templates.
switchMap chains dependent calls; forkJoin runs calls in parallel.
Subject / BehaviorSubject let you push values; signals are often simpler for state.
